x: The first world conference on the environment was held at Stockholm in 1972 (UNCHE). Rio (1992) was the Earth Summit and Johannesburg (2002) Rio+10.
t: Arrange the environment summits in time order.

x: Option B is incorrect: UNEP came out of the 1972 Stockholm Conference, not the 1992 Rio summit. It is headquartered in Nairobi.
t: Match UNEP to the conference it came from.

x: Both are true: the UNFCCC was adopted at Rio in 1992 and came into force on 21 March 1994. Its adoption does not explain its start date, so R does not explain A.
t: Discriminate the year adopted from the year in force.

x: The UNCCD covers desertification, the CBD biodiversity conservation, Cartagena biosafety and GMOs, and Nagoya access and benefit sharing. The answer is a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.
t: Match each treaty to its subject.

x: All four are correct: the Ramsar Convention on wetlands was signed on 2 February 1971, 2 February is World Wetlands Day, and its principle is the wise use of wetlands.
t: Recall the Ramsar facts.
s:
Consider the following statements:

I. The Ramsar Convention was signed on February 2nd, 1971.
II. The Ramsar Convention concerns wetlands.
III. World Wetlands Day is observed on February 2nd.
IV. The principle of the Ramsar Convention is conservation and wise or sustainable use.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Stockholm was the UN Conference on the Human Environment, Rio+5 was held in New York (1997), Rio+10 in Johannesburg (2002), and Rio+20 in Rio (2012). The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Arrange the Rio follow-ups in time order.

x: Both are true: World Environment Day falls on 5 June, the date the Stockholm Conference opened, and was first held in 1973.
t: Recall World Environment Day.

x: Both are true: the UNFCCC aims to stabilise greenhouse gas concentrations, and COP stands for Conference of Parties. A short name does not explain an aim, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether an expansion explains an aim.

x: All four are correct: the UNCCD (1994) links environment, development and land management, works bottom-up with local communities, and is tied to SDG 15 and Land Degradation Neutrality.
t: Recall the UNCCD.
s:
Consider the following statements regarding the UNCCD:
I. It was established in 1994.
II. It links environment with development and sustainable land management.
III. It follows a bottom-up approach and involves local-community participation.
IV. It is linked with SDG 15 and Land Degradation Neutrality.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Three are correct: the CBD was adopted at Rio in 1992 and covers sustainable use and benefit sharing. Statement 4 is false because the CBD was not adopted in 2014.
t: Recall the CBD year.

x: The Nagoya Protocol on access and benefit sharing was adopted in 2010 at CBD COP-10 in Nagoya, Japan. It entered into force in 2014, which is the trap.
t: Separate the year of adoption from the year of entry into force.

x: The Ramsar Convention takes its name from Ramsar, Iran, where it was signed in 1971.
t: Recall where Ramsar was signed.

x: Montreal dates from 1987, Kyoto 1997, Cartagena 2000, and Minamata 2013. The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
t: Arrange the treaties in time order.

x: Option C is incorrect: the GEF's first implementing partners were UNDP, UNEP and the World Bank. The CBD is a convention it funds.
t: Discriminate GEF partners from GEF-funded conventions.

x: Both are true and R explains A: the GEF funds five conventions, Minamata among them, so it is a financial mechanism for the Minamata Convention.
t: Check whether the general rule in R covers the particular case in A.
s:
Assertion (A): The Global Environment Facility serves as a financial mechanism for the Minamata Convention on mercury.
Reason (R): The Global Environment Facility is the financial mechanism for five conventions: Minamata, Stockholm, CBD, UNCCD and UNFCCC.

x: The WMO, a UN agency for weather and water, is headquartered in Geneva.
t: Match each institution to its city.

x: Only I is correct: the New York Declaration on Forests was endorsed at the 2014 UN Climate Summit. It is voluntary, not binding, and India was not among the first signatories.
t: Watch for 'legally binding'.
s:
Consider the following statements about the New York Declaration on Forests:
I. It was first endorsed at the UN Climate Summit in 2014.
II. It is legally binding.
III. India was an initial signatory.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Montreal deals with ozone, Kyoto (1997) set binding emission cuts for developed countries, Paris (2015) covers climate change for all, and Stockholm (2001) targets persistent organic pollutants. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Use the adoption years to separate the two climate treaties.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Montreal Protocol
(b) Kyoto Protocol
(c) Paris Agreement
(d) Stockholm Convention

List-II
(i) Ozone depletion
(ii) Adopted in 1997 with binding emission cuts for developed countries
(iii) Adopted in 2015 and targets climate change
(iv) Adopted in 2001 and targets persistent organic pollutants (POPs)

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:

x: All four are correct: Minamata covers mercury, Cartagena biosafety and LMOs, and Nagoya (2010) genetic resources and benefit sharing.
t: Match each treaty to its subject.

x: India both gives money to the Global Environment Facility and receives grants from it.
t: Recall India's GEF role.

x: Both are true: the WMO grew from the International Meteorological Organization (1873) and became the WMO in 1951, and it works on meteorology and hydrology. Its field does not explain its history, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a field explains a history.

x: The New York Declaration on Forests aims to halt or reduce global forest loss.
t: Recall the declaration's aim.

x: All four groups back the New York Declaration on Forests: governments, companies, civil society and indigenous groups.
t: Recall who signed the declaration.

x: The 1972 UN Conference on the Human Environment was held at Stockholm. It was the first major global environmental conference.
t: Recall the Stockholm conference.

x: Option A is incorrect: the 1952 Forest Policy's classes were national, protected and village forests, plus tree-lands. National parks were not one of them.
t: Recall the 1952 forest classes.

x: Both are true: the Green Climate Fund was set up at COP16 in Cancún in 2010, and COP16 was held there that year. Restating where and when does not explain why, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether R adds a reason.

x: The Indian Forest Act, 1927, sets the forest legal framework, the WPA, 1972, protects wildlife, the FCA, 1980, controls diversion of forest land, and the EPA, 1986, protects the environment. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Match each Act to its subject.

x: All four are correct: the 1988 Policy promoted afforestation and wasteland development, set one-third cover nationally and two-thirds in hills, and stressed community participation.
t: Recall the 1988 Forest Policy targets.
s:
Consider the following statements about the National Forest Policy, 1988:

I. It promoted afforestation and wasteland development.
II. It targeted forest/tree cover over one-third of the country's geographical area.
III. It set a two-thirds forest/tree-cover target for mountain and hilly areas.
IV. Community participation was a major thrust.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Both are true: reserved forests are the most restricted, where activities are banned unless permitted, and protected forests are more regulated than unclassed forests.
t: Rank reserved, protected and unclassed forests.

x: The order is the Earth Summit (1992), Earth Summit +5 (1997), Rio+10/WSSD (2002) and Rio+20/UNCSD (2012). The answer is A, B, C, D.
t: Arrange the Rio follow-ups in time order.

x: Both are true: the UN Conference on the Human Environment was held in 1972 and was the first major global environmental conference.
t: Recall the Stockholm conference.

x: The Earth Summit (Rio) gave Agenda 21, Earth Summit +5 (New York) reviewed progress, Rio+10 (Johannesburg) focused on sustainable development, and Rio+20 gave 'The Future We Want'. The answer is a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i.
t: Match each summit to its city and outcome.

x: COP27 was held at Sharm el-Sheikh (2022), COP28 Dubai (2023), COP29 Baku (2024, the finance COP), and COP30 Belém (2025). The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
t: Arrange the recent COPs in time order.

x: Both are true: CBD COP10 was held in 2010, and COP means Conference of Parties. A short name does not explain a date, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether an expansion explains a date.

x: CBD COP10 was held at Nagoya (2010), COP11 Hyderabad (2012), COP12 Pyeongchang (2014), and COP13 Cancún (2016). The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Arrange the CBD COPs in time order.

x: All three are correct: CBD COP14 was held at Sharm el-Sheikh (2018), COP15 at Kunming and Montreal (2021–22), and COP16 at Cali (2024).
t: Arrange the CBD COPs in time order.
s:
Consider the following statements:

I. CBD COP 14 was held in 2018 at Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt.
II. CBD COP 15 was held during 2021–22 in Kunming and Montreal.
III. CBD COP 16 was held in 2024 at Cali, Colombia.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Stockholm (1972) dealt with the human environment, Rio (1992) was the Earth Summit, Kyoto (1997) dealt with climate change, and Johannesburg (2002) with sustainable development. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Arrange the conferences in time order.

x: Both are true: Paris (2015) produced the Paris Agreement, and Glasgow (2021, COP26) is where India announced Panchamrit.
t: Recall the Paris and Glasgow outcomes.

x: The Green Climate Fund helps developing countries cut emissions and adapt to climate change.
t: Recall what the Green Climate Fund does.

x: Option C is incorrect: the Green Climate Fund was formally set up at COP16 in Cancún (2010), not at Durban.
t: Recall where the GCF was set up.

x: A is true and B is false: the 1952 Policy included tree-lands as a class, but national parks were not one of its classes.
t: Recall the 1952 forest classes.

x: All three are correct: the 1988 Policy promoted reforestation, wood substitutes and alternative fuels, and aimed at ecological stability.
t: Recall the 1988 Forest Policy.
s:
Consider the following statements about the National Forest Policy of 1988:
I. It promoted reforestation and replantation.
II. It encouraged wood substitutes and alternative fuel.
III. It aimed at ecological stability.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Unclassed forests are those outside the reserved and protected classes, and they are the least regulated.
t: Rank reserved, protected and unclassed forests.

x: The Forest Rights Act, 2006, recognises the rights of forest-dwelling communities. The 1927, 1980 and 1972 options describe other Acts.
t: Match each forest Act to its year.

x: Afforestation plants trees on land never forested, reforestation restores lost forest, social forestry grows trees for community needs, and community participation brings local people into management, as in Joint Forest Management. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Separate new planting from replanting, then the two people-centred ideas.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
 a. Afforestation
 b. Reforestation
 c. Social forestry
 d. Community participation

List-II
 i. Involving local people in forest management, as in Joint Forest Management
 ii. Planting trees on land that was not forested before
 iii. Re-establishment of forest cover where forests have been depleted
 iv. Tree or forest development aimed at local or community needs and reducing pressure on natural forests
